lawyer: Mr. K.S. Zaman, Advocate ----- for the petitioners
parties:
The Manager, Uttara Bank Limited ------- Petitioners
Vs.
Srimoti Madhabi Rani Kundu ------- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Saha, J: This application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against the judgment and decree dated 30.6.99 passed by the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Natore in Title Appeal No. 155 of 1997 affirming the judgment and decree dated 2.10.89 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Lalpur in the District of Natore in Other Suit No. 100 of 1995 decreeing the suit. 

 4. The petitioner defendants contested the suit by filing written statements denying all material allegations of the plaint and contended inter alia that the plaintiff as a housewife was not eligible for opening D.P.S. A/C. as per terms and conditions of the scheme. It has also been contended that the plaintiff defaulted in making payment of monthly installment for the month of April, 1998 and thereby she forfeited her right to continue the account as per condition 8(1) of the scheme. It has also been alleged that subsequent acceptance of her defaulted installment for May, 1989 with fine by the Branch Manager without obtaining prior permission from the central Management of the Bank was beyond his power and authority and as such it is not binding upon the Bank. It has been also contended that at the time of opening the Account rate of interest was 16% per annum but subsequently the rate of interest was lowered from 16% to 10%, causing heavy losses to the bank on the D.P.S. Account and consequently any defaulting account holder is not entitled to the benefit of the scheme and. therefore, she has no right to continue her account like other defaulting account-holders. It was further contended that Uttara Bank limited is a private bank and the account in question is just an ordinary contract between the contending parties and for the alleged back of the contract in connection in respect of the D.P.S. account of the plaint, action for damages may be lie but no suit for declaration of her right to continue her account under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act is contemplated in law. The plaintiff is not also entitled to a decree directing the defendants to continue the disputed D.P.S. Account. 

 6. The learned Senior Assistant Judge on consideration of the materials before him was pleased by the impugned judgment dated 2.10.97 to decree the suit. Against the aforesaid decree the defendant petitioner took an appeal before the District Judge, Natore being Title Appeal No. 155 of 1997. Subsequently the said appeal was transferred to the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Natore for disposal and the learned Subordinate Judge by his impugned judgment dated 30.6.99 dismissed the suit and affirmed the decree passed by the learned trial Court. It is against the aforesaid judgment and decree the petitioners preferred this application before this Court. 

 5. Mr. K.S. Zaman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that in view of the fact that the defendant bank is a private bank the relationship between the plaintiff and the defendant bank is one of the nature of ordinary business transaction based on a contract and as such for any violation of such a contract, there can be no suit for declaration the plaintiffs right to continue the disputed D.P.S. Account and as such learned Courts below erred in law in decreeing the suit in violation of the provision of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and the same has occasioned failure of justice. The learned Advocate further argues that if there has been a violation of the contract relating to the disputed D.P.S. Account, action for damages is the appropriate remedy and there can be no order for mandatory injunction and as such the learned Courts below erred in law in passing the impugned judgments on erroneous view of law occasioning failure of justice.
